defects.title: NFC_IRQ is bound in the netlist. The drawing half is stale and cannot be re-judged from the frozen source.
defects.detail:
NETLIST — RESOLVED, no defect. But NOT by the argument offered in the hand-off, which was that NFC_IRQ's absence from the single-pin-network list proves it reaches a host. That inference does not hold: the DRC rule reads 'is a single network connected to only ONE component pin', and this lane's own measurement already put TWO pins on NFC_IRQ (U12-NFC.27 and R43-NFC.2). A two-pin net can never trip that rule, whether or not the ESP is on it, so the absence is CONSISTENT WITH but does not PROVE the conclusion. The load-bearing evidence in the same log is different and stronger: U9-ESP has ZERO floating pins, down from 18-19, and the only two single-pin networks on the whole board are $1N153914 and BUCK_PG, neither NFC-related. All 41 U9-ESP pins are therefore on multi-pin nets. Combined with the name-to-net map that puts pin 4 (IO4) on NFC_IRQ, the net is bound. No defect.

DRAWING — STALE, and this lane will not call it either way. The drawing finding was measured against frozen source 489736:464c27d4. Between the 12:17 DRC and the 14:58 DRC, U9-ESP went from 18-19 floating pins to ZERO, so something was repaired in the live document. This lane has no post-repair source read, so it can claim neither that the displaced stubs were fixed nor that they persist. The earlier 'DRAWING: real' wording is withdrawn as unsupported against current live. If the visible-wiring question still matters, re-run harness/check_schematic_connectivity.py against a fresh source export — it is a two-minute measurement.

defects.detail: RFO2 (pin 15) and RFI2 (pin 23) are unconnected and no NFC_RFO2 or NFC_RFI2 net exists. This is now understood to be a VALID ST single-ended topology, not a wiring omission: AN5592 Figure 3 shows only RFO1 and RFI1, and ST support states that in single-ended operation only RFO1/RFI1 is connected to the antenna and driven. What is missing is everything attached to that choice. The device DEFAULTS to differential (IO configuration register 1 bit single = 0), so the board cannot work until firmware sets single = 1 with rfo2 = 0, and no repository document records that. No decision-register entry chooses single-ended over differential. The datasheet states the trade-off plainly: single driver mode halves the antenna LC tank component count and cost but reduces output power, and AN5592 adds that a single-ended signal is unbalanced and more prone to noise and interference.

AN5276 sec 3.3 requires the filter cutoff to be between 8 and 17 MHz and specifically NOT between 13 and 14 MHz, because a cutoff near the 13.56 MHz carrier collapses the system Q factor. Neither fitted value is close to a workable pair: holding C59 at 22 pF would need roughly 4 to 18 uH, and holding L2 at 5.6 nH would need roughly 16 to 71 nF. Both values are wrong together, which reads as a copied set rather than a derived one. The filter as fitted does not attenuate the push-pull driver harmonics it exists to remove.

architecture_decision_required.status: NEEDS CAPTAIN RULING AND A DECISION-REGISTER ENTRY
architecture_decision_required.why_not_settled_here: This is an architecture choice, not a repair. It changes the component count, the achievable read range, the firmware register setup, and whether antenna diagnostics exist at all. This lane records the evidence and a recommendation; it does not implement either topology.
architecture_decision_required.recommendation: Ratify SINGLE-ENDED WITH CABLE (AN5592 sec 2.3), which is what the board already is.
evidence_for: The K1 antenna is external and remote on a U.FL coaxial lead. AN5592 sec 2.3 is the ST topology for exactly that, and ST support directs a STEVAL-ST25R3916B user with an external antenna on a coaxial cable to AN5592, confirming it applies to the ST25R3916B.
Differential over a coaxial lead is not what AN5592 documents; the cable case is presented only in the single-ended family.

AAT is unavailable either way here: AN5592 sec 2.4 states AAT is not possible for a single-ended antenna with cable because any change in cable parameters detunes the reader. K1 already leaves AAT_A and AAT_B unconnected, so nothing is lost by ratifying.
The EXT_LM removal that AN5592 requires for single-ended on ST25R3916 devices is already satisfied: K1 has no EXT_LM circuit.
Fewer components and less board area, per AN5592 sec 2.2 and the datasheet sec 4.2.1.
evidence_against_and_costs: Reduced output power. Datasheet sec 4.2.1: single driver mode halves the antenna LC tank component count and cost 'but also the output power is reduced'. Read range is the thing being traded.
AN5592 sec 2.2: a single-ended signal is unbalanced and 'more prone to noise and interference'. On a board carrying a switching buck, LED drivers and USB, that matters.
AN5276 sec 2 recommends the differential design for low-power applications 'because gives the best range'.

Part of the receive path is given up: the peak detector reads RFI1 only at gain 0.7 while the AM demodulator mixer uses both inputs at gain 0.55, and the amplitude and phase detectors are differential between RFI1 and RFI2.
AN5592 sec 2.3: the cable case admits only a limited set of target matching impedances, for example 4, 8 and 16 ohm, so there is less design freedom.
A second matching network is required at the antenna end, tuned to the cable characteristic impedance. That is a part of the product that does not exist yet and is not in any BOM.
architecture_decision_required.if_captain_rules_differential_instead: Then NFC-D4 becomes a real wiring defect again and RFO2, RFI2 and a second CVDR1/CVDR2 divider pair must all be added, with a second EMC inductor and a second Cs/Cp arm. That is a larger change than the single-ended repair and it is not the topology AN5592 documents for a coaxial lead.
architecture_decision_required.firmware_consequence_either_way: IO configuration register 1 bit single must be set to 1 with bit rfo2 = 0 for the as-built board. The device default is differential. This belongs in contracts/nfc-interface.md whichever way the ruling goes.

independent_anchors: Pins 1,2,3 are named GND, 3V3, EN and land on GND, 3V3, ESP_EN — three consecutive power/enable matches.

Pin 13 'IO19' -> USB_DM_S3 and pin 14 'IO20' -> USB_DP_S3. ESP32-S3 GPIO19 and GPIO20 ARE the native USB D- and D+ pins; this is a hardware fact, not a naming coincidence, and a two-pitch error would break it.
